questions.q: Which three real headers does an authenticated Messages API request carry?
questions.explain: x-api-key authenticates the request, anthropic-version pins the API version, and content-type declares the JSON body.

questions.q: What does a stop_reason of max_tokens tell your application?
options: The reply was cut off and is incomplete
The reply finished naturally and is complete
The model is waiting for a tool result
questions.explain: max_tokens means generation hit the cap before finishing naturally — the response should be treated as incomplete, unlike end_turn.

questions.q: Which stage of the request lifecycle happens before any model inference, catching a malformed body or bad API key fast and cheaply?
questions.explain: Validation checks the request shape and credentials before any model work begins, so bad requests fail quickly.

questions.q: Which two HTTP error codes are generally safe to retry automatically with exponential backoff?
questions.explain: 500 (api_error) and 529 (overloaded_error) represent transient server-side issues — the official SDKs retry these with backoff by default.

questions.q: What does every error response from the API include, alongside the error type and message?
questions.explain: Every error response carries a request_id (matching the request-id response header) that you'd reference when contacting support.
